$description: The chart decision tree: the single source for the agent's docs/chart-decision-tree.md, mckviz.suggest() and the guide's chooser. Three questions in order: what is in the data (shape), what should the reader see (question), then start with a chart and go further when a condition holds; color comes from what it encodes. Built by tools/build_chooser.py (run by tokens/build.py).

triggers.clustered: values bunched far from zero (the smallest is more than half the largest)
triggers.wide_range: the largest value is more than 20 times the smallest
triggers.has_size: a count column (headcount, employees, moves) whose values differ a lot (largest at least 5 times the smallest)
triggers.rate_and_size: the measure is a rate or share and there is a count column, so rate × count gives an absolute amount
triggers.has_benchmark: a benchmark: a column that is the same on every row, one named target / benchmark / average, or a Total row
triggers.tight_spread: most categories sit close together (the middle half spans less than a fifth of the range)
triggers.parts_ordered: the parts have a natural order (bands, ratings, unfavorable to favorable)
triggers.parts_over_time: the measures are parts that add up to 100 in each period
triggers.two_units: two measures in different units over the same periods
triggers.has_target: a target or goal to compare against
triggers.several_numbers: several headline numbers side by side
triggers.counts_not_rates: the values are counts, not rates
triggers.gap_is_point: the difference itself is the story (a gap column, or the pair is us vs. a benchmark)

focus.name: Focus (default)
focus.when: The headline names a few items: everything grey, those items McKesson Blue (usually one or two; when most would be blue, none stands out). Bold the matching labels.
focus.how: mv.highlight(labels, focus=...); a stack: mv.hstack(..., story=...)

uniform_accent.name: Uniform + accent
uniform_accent.when: Every item belongs to the same story and one exception must pop: the series light blue, the exception navy.
uniform_accent.how: mv.highlight(labels, accent=..., base=C.focus_light); a stack: mv.hstack(..., accent=..., uniform=True)

focus_accent.name: Focus + accent
focus_accent.when: The headline names a group and one member that stands out above the rest of it: grey context, the group McKesson Blue, the standout navy ("Four support roles are above 50% exposure, led by Claims & Billing"). Use it for a "led by" or "most of all" clause. Two items the headline names as equals ("two job families") stay Focus: both blue.
focus_accent.how: mv.highlight(labels, focus=..., accent=...); a stack: mv.hstack(..., story=..., accent=...)

story_greys.name: Story segment + greys
story_greys.when: Focus applied to a stack: the one part that is the story blue on the baseline, the other parts in context greys.

categorical.name: Categorical
categorical.when: Every series or part matters and must be told apart: at most 6, always in the fixed order (blue, navy, bright blue, teal, mint, orange); prefer 4 or fewer.

sequential.name: Sequential
sequential.when: One ordered measure or ordered bands (low to high, bands of a rate): light to dark in one hue. Darker means more.

diverging.name: Diverging
diverging.when: Values centered on zero or a target: orange below (worse), blue above, a neutral middle.

steps.name: Ordered steps
steps.when: Process stages in order (blue to green), never for magnitude.

status.name: Status only
status.when: On track / at risk / off track / not started / done, always with a symbol and a word, never on data series.

shapes.label: One number, or a few
shapes.looks_like: A single row, or a handful of headline figures.

questions.ask: What one figure should they remember?

further.chart: Progress bar or ring toward the target
KPI row

shapes.label: One measure per person or team (many rows)
shapes.looks_like: Many rows, one per person or team, with a measure (compa-ratio, span of control, tenure) and maybe a group column.

questions.ask: How spread out is it? What's typical? Where are the outliers?

further.chart: Strip or box plot by group, the focus group in blue

questions.ask: What share of each group is beyond a threshold (below 0.90, over the span limit, under 1 year)?

start.chart: Sorted bar of each group's share beyond the threshold, with its n

further.chart: Strip plot by group, the zone beyond the threshold shaded
further.only_if: the headline is about the spread or the outliers, not only the share

questions.avoid: A count of people beyond the line with no group size

shapes.label: Categories × one measure
shapes.looks_like: One row per category (job family, site, role) with a measure, maybe a count column and a benchmark.

questions.ask: Which is biggest, and by how much? How do they rank?

further.chart: Dot plot
further.why: bars must start at zero, which hides small differences

further.chart: Proportional bubbles, or split the chart
Sorted bar with the tail grouped into Other
Bubble strip: position = the measure, bubble area = the count
further.why: shows how close the categories are and how many people each one covers
further.only_if: the headline is about how many people each one covers, not only the rate

further.chart: Bubble strip with only the outliers and largest named

color_switch.when: the headline names a group and one member stands out
every item is part of the story and one is the exception

questions.ask: How far is each from the benchmark?

further.chart: Dot plot with a labelled benchmark line

questions.ask: Where is the most of it in absolute terms (rate × people)?

start.chart: Sorted bar of the derived count, footnoted as an estimate

further.chart: Treemap: tile area = the count, shade = the rate
further.why: people and the rate in one picture
further.only_if: the headline is about the volume and the rate together

questions.avoid: A derived count presented as a recorded one

color_switch.when: the headline names a group and one member stands out

questions.ask: What are the exact figures for each, so readers can find their own row?

start.chart: Blended table: an inline bar for the count, the measure as a heat column, bold focus rows, a weighted total

questions.avoid: A plain grid of numbers with no highlight

shapes.label: Parts of a whole
shapes.looks_like: Columns that add up to 100 (or to a total) in every row: workforce mix, survey favorability, time mix.

questions.ask: What is each made of, and how do the mixes compare?

further.chart: One 100% bar, or a donut with 5 slices or fewer
Treemap, or group the small parts into Other
100% stacked bar in sequential shades (diverging for unfavorable to favorable)

color_switch.when: a group of parts is the story and one stands out
every part matters and one is the exception

shapes.label: A bridge from one total to another
shapes.looks_like: Steps with a kind column (total, delta): headcount bridge, labor cost bridge.

questions.ask: What moved the total from A to B?
questions.avoid: Two stacked bars side by side

shapes.label: A pair of values per category
shapes.looks_like: Before and after (rank_2023 and rank_2026, FY25 and FY26) or us and them (internal and market pay) for each category, or a period column with two values.

questions.ask: What changed for each, or how big is each gap?

further.chart: Slope chart of the ranks
further.only_if: the headline is about who moved up or down the ranking

further.chart: Slope chart
further.only_if: the headline is about the direction of change more than the size of each value

further.chart: Diverging bars of the difference
Dumbbell with a target line
further.only_if: the headline is about the gap to the target

questions.avoid: Two separate bar charts the reader must compare

color_switch.when: the headline names a group and one member stands out

questions.ask: What are the before and after values, and the change, for each?

start.chart: Blended table: before, after, and a change column with the unfavorable direction in orange

questions.avoid: A change column with no sign

shapes.label: Categories × several measures
shapes.looks_like: One row per category with two or more measures in different units (a scorecard; pay vs. exposure).

start.chart: Scatter; bubble scatter when a count can be the bubble area

further.chart: Two aligned bar charts, one per measure

color_switch.when: the headline names a group and one member stands out

questions.ask: How does each category score across all the measures?

start.chart: Blended table (scorecard): inline bars, one or two heat columns, a change column

further.chart: Parallel coordinates, the focus line in blue
Blended table with the gap to the benchmark as a diverging column
further.only_if: readers need each score against the benchmark, not only the scores

shapes.label: Two sets of categories × one measure
shapes.looks_like: A long table: business unit × driver, function × quarter, with one value per pair.

questions.ask: Where are the hot spots across both dimensions?

further.chart: Diverging heat table around the benchmark

color_switch.when: values centered on zero or a target

shapes.label: A measure over time
shapes.looks_like: A period column (months, quarters, years) with three or more periods, maybe a series column.

questions.ask: How is it moving? When did it change?

start.chart: Line, the focus series in blue and the rest grey

further.chart: Small multiples on one shared scale
Stacked area, or 100% columns for a few periods
Two aligned panels (never dual axes)
Line with a labelled target line

color_switch.when: the headline names a group and one member stands out

shapes.label: Flows from one state to another
shapes.looks_like: From and to columns with a count: internal moves, pipeline stages.

questions.ask: Where do people go, and how many?

color_switch.when: the stages are a process in order

shapes.label: Places
shapes.looks_like: A state, country, county or FIPS column.

questions.ask: Where is it? Does place matter?

further.chart: Bubble map (counts never go on a choropleth)

shapes.label: Plans and status
shapes.looks_like: Workstreams with start and end dates, milestones, owners or a status column.

questions.ask: What happens when, who owns it, and is it on track?

further.chart: Initiative tracker with a status column

shapes.label: Overlapping groups
shapes.looks_like: Yes/no (1/0) membership columns with a count per combination.

questions.ask: How much do the groups overlap?

further.chart: Sorted bar of the combinations

questions.avoid: A Venn with 4 or more sets
